title: Total Score of Dungeon Runs
summary: Given a positive integer health point (hp) and two positive 1-indexed integer arrays damage and requirement, where damage[i] represents the health reduction upon entering room i, and requirement[i] is the minimum health needed to earn 1 point for that room, calculate the total score.
statement: Given a positive integer health point (hp) and two positive 1-indexed integer arrays damage and requirement, where damage[i] represents the health reduction upon entering room i, and requirement[i] is the minimum health needed to earn 1 point for that room, calculate the total score. The score for starting at room j is the number of points earned by entering rooms j through n in order, with hp health points initially. The total score is the sum of scores for starting at each room from 1 to n. You must enter each room in sequence and can finish even if your health points become non-positive.
constraints: damage and requirement have equal length up to 100,000 and all values are positive.
For every starting room j, enter all rooms j..n; room i scores when health after its damage is at least requirement[i].
Return the sum of scores over every starting room.
hints: For a fixed room i and start j, remaining health is hp-(prefix[i]-prefix[j-1]).
Rearrange the scoring condition to prefix[j-1]≥prefix[i]+requirement[i]-hp.
Damage prefixes are strictly increasing, so binary-search the first qualifying start boundary among prefixes before i and count the suffix.
Summing these counts by scored room is equivalent to summing scores by starting room.
editorial: Summing these counts by scored room is equivalent to summing scores by starting room.

tests.explanation: Across all starts, rooms earn a total of three points.
Only starting at the second room earns a point, so the total is one.
